profile.reading: This OSM record, "Tahoe Reno 5," is mapped to Switch's "Citadel Campus" in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, Storey County, Nevada, sharing the same 1 Superloop Circle address as the other numbered Tahoe Reno buildings in this dataset, but could not be confirmed as an individually named or specified Switch facility this session. Switch's own website, full press-release archive, and its FY2021 SEC 10-K filing, its last as a public company before the 2022 DigitalBridge/IFM take-private transaction, name and give specifications only for Tahoe Reno 1 (opened, 1.3 million-plus square feet, 130 megawatts) and, at a groundbreaking stage with no individual specs, Tahoe Reno 2 and 3; no Switch press release, SEC filing, or campus page found this session names a "Tahoe Reno 5" specifically. The FY2021 10-K discloses seven future facilities in aggregate (5.89 million square feet, 520 megawatts combined) without individually naming or numbering them, which likely explains why third-party mapping data assigns sequential "Tahoe Reno 4" and "Tahoe Reno 5" labels, since these appear to be placeholder or extrapolated labels applied by mapping or aggregator sources rather than confirmed Switch-published building names. This profile does not assert that a building called "Tahoe Reno 5" specifically exists as a distinct, confirmed structure separate from the campus's undifferentiated future-facility total, consistent with this dataset's practice of flagging genuine ambiguity rather than guessing. Switch's current marketing describes the full Citadel Campus at up to 17.4 million square feet and more than 2 gigawatts of power at completion, roughly three times the megawatt figure and more than double the square footage Switch cited for the same campus as recently as 2021, reflecting a major post-acquisition re-scoping of the site's ambitions.

reading.body:
"Tahoe Reno 5" is a placeholder label applied by aggregator sources to an unconfirmed Switch building at the Citadel Campus in McCarran, Nevada. Switch's own publications name only Tahoe Reno 1 (which opened with 130 megawatts and 1.3 million square feet) and reference Tahoe Reno 2 and 3 at groundbreaking stage; no Switch press release, SEC filing, or website names a "Tahoe Reno 5" as a distinct facility with its own specifications. The FY2021 10-K discloses seven future facilities at the site only in aggregate (520 megawatts combined), leaving individual building identities and power allocations unpublished.

Switch's current marketing describes the full Citadel Campus target as 2 gigawatts of power capacity and 17.4 million square feet at completion, a major expansion from the roughly 650 megawatts and 7.2 million square feet the operator cited in 2021. The campus holds a Switch proprietary "Tier 5 Platinum" rating, not a third-party certification. Nevada as a whole has 26 mapped data center facilities but only 2 with published power specifications totaling 10.37 megawatts in the state registry, so most Nevada capacity remains undisclosed.

Without individual specifications for "Tahoe Reno 5," its materiality to AI infrastructure cannot be assessed from published facts. The Citadel Campus at full build-out would rank substantially by scale, but the distribution of its 2-gigawatt target across individual buildings and their completion timeline remain unknown. Readers tracking power constraints on AI scaling should note that Nevada's largest projects remain largely unspecified in public sources.
